chapter: Louis Armstrong, Basie and New York studio scene
title: Billy Taylor Sr., Beverly Peer and other bassists, plus how Taylor became Billy
summary: Taylor and Hinton recall the first black CBS bassists, including Billy Taylor Sr., and the Chick Webb pianist Taylor loved.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Maybe he came later.
He came later but in „39 he was with Duke because [unintelligible] was there.
Right.
Because he just walked away.
That‟s right he just walked away from the job.
He went to Washington and worked in the Post Office for quite some time.
But he worked, both he and his son, he had a son named Billy Jr. that played. And they both, I don‟t know it was kind of tragic because I thought they both were excellent players.
Absolutely they were.

People never really…I played with Billy Senior. As a mater of fact he is the reason that people call me Billy instead of Bill. I mean I was always called Bill until I came to New York. And when I got the job with Ben Webster they asked me what my name was I said Bill Taylor. So when I went to work they put everybody‟s name outside. So when I went to work it said, Billy. I went in and I said, “Is Billy Taylor here?” The guy looked at me and said, “You told me that was your name.” I said oh okay.
That‟s right. Yeah they were…that was the main bass players that were around. Beverly Pier was a good…
Beverly Pier yeah.
Beverly Pier was a bass player with Chick Webb.
And he now works with Bobby Short.
Bobby Short, yeah. I vote for him every year.
There was a guy with Chick Webb‟s band who was a wonderful pianist and I have been trying to thin of his name, Tommy Something.
I don‟t know.

See every time I see Ella I mean to ask her because she would know. But I was so impressed by this guy‟s playing. Chick had a small group called, I forget what he called them but they used to play in a Spanish town, the small band things, Chancy Horton and some of the other guys.
Oh yeah.
And this guy, I just loved the way he played piano. He was one of those younger guys that didn‟t sound like anybody that I had heard.
There were some great musicians in those days.
